guide.title: Mendelssohn: String Quartet No.2, Op.13 – III. Intermezzo (Allegretto con moto)
guide.overview: This is a movement in A minor, in a light 2/4 beat. It opens with a soft main tune in the first violin. A very quiet, fast middle section follows, then a long wandering section. The opening tune comes back near the end. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat them as a guide. Lead-part labels are also a best guess.

listening_points.headline: The main tune, soft in the first violin
listening_points.text: The movement starts softly with the main tune in Violin 1 [m. 1-3]. The other parts move with it in block-like harmony. The tune repeats at [m. 5-7]. This section is marked to be repeated.

listening_points.headline: A step to E minor
listening_points.text: The music moves to E minor [m. 10-18]. Violin 1 sings over an accompaniment. Near the end the lines become more independent [m. 16-17].

listening_points.headline: The opening tune returns
listening_points.text: Back in A minor, the main tune returns in Violin 1 at the same pitch as at the start [m. 19-21]. It comes once more at [m. 23-25]. Listen for the familiar shape from the opening.

listening_points.headline: Sudden hush: viola alone, very soft
listening_points.text: A new, faster section begins (Allegro di molto). The mood changes suddenly. The dynamic drops to very soft. The viola plays by itself [m. 27-30]. The key estimate brightens to E major from [m. 28].

listening_points.headline: Whispering block harmony in E major
listening_points.text: The parts now move together in block harmony [m. 31-45]. It stays very soft. The lead passes from Violin 2 to Violin 1, but the labels are uncertain, so the lead is probably shared. Keys shift quickly through C# minor and G# minor before E major returns.

listening_points.headline: A lift to B major
listening_points.text: The key moves up to B major [m. 46-49]. One part carries the melody while the others accompany. Then the lines become independent [m. 50] as the key returns to E major.

listening_points.headline: Part 4 begins; Violin 2 leads at first
listening_points.text: A longer section starts, back at soft volume [m. 51]. Violin 2 leads at first, with high confidence [m. 51-54]. Violin 1 takes over at [m. 56]. The key turns to B minor [m. 53]. The analysis marks [m. 55] as the loudest or busiest point. That is a computer estimate. The marking there is still soft.

listening_points.headline: Wandering through D major and F# minor
listening_points.text: The keys shift often: D major [m. 59], F# minor [m. 62], then B minor again [m. 66]. The lead moves between parts, and some labels are uncertain. Most of this is melody with accompaniment. The sound becomes very soft at [m. 72].

listening_points.headline: Independent lines, then Db major and C# minor
listening_points.text: The parts play more separate lines [m. 75-80]. The key reaches Db major [m. 78]. Then it moves to C# minor [m. 83]. At [m. 84] the parts play in unison or octaves, meaning the same notes at the same or different heights.

listening_points.headline: A major, then E major with swelling and fading
listening_points.text: The key brightens to A major [m. 87], then E major [m. 95]. Over [m. 96-99] the markings alternate between getting louder and getting softer. Listen for these small waves. The block harmony continues, with Violin 1 probably leading.

listening_points.headline: A quiet stretch, then a short link to A minor
listening_points.text: Melody with accompaniment takes over [m. 104-116]. The sound is very soft, then steps up to soft at [m. 107]. A short new section (allegro moderato) begins at [m. 112]. It leads the harmony back toward A minor [m. 115].

listening_points.headline: The main tune comes home
listening_points.text: The last section opens in A minor with the main tune in Violin 1 [m. 117-119]. It repeats at [m. 121-123]. These are at the same pitch as the opening. The sound is soft.

listening_points.headline: The E minor passage returns; the tune appears at its first pitch
listening_points.text: Material like the earlier E minor passage comes back [m. 124-136]. It includes independent lines near [m. 132-133]. The main tune shows up in Violin 1 at [m. 135-137] and again at [m. 139-141]. Those are the same pitch as the opening, though the local key labels say E minor and D minor.

listening_points.headline: A brighter A major, with sudden drops to very soft
listening_points.text: The key turns to A major [m. 140]. The sound drops suddenly to very soft at [m. 141]. It changes again suddenly at [m. 143] and [m. 145]. Violin 1 plays alone at [m. 146] and [m. 150].

listening_points.headline: A hushed ending in A minor
listening_points.text: The parts play the same line in unison or octaves [m. 152-155], with the viola leading. A fading marking appears at [m. 153]. The key settles in A minor from [m. 157]. The movement ends very softly with block harmony [m. 164].

glossary.explanation: The opening tune in Violin 1. It is the tune to listen for when it comes back.
The home note and scale of a passage. Minor often sounds darker. Major often sounds brighter.
A move from one key to another.
The parts move together in block-like harmony.
One part sings the tune while the others support it.
Parts play the same notes, at the same or different heights.
